Variants.Content: Shipwrecks can be caused by storms, reefs, collisions, fires, overloading or wrong headings. The cold after falling into the water, the broken ship's wood, the shore current and whether there are people nearby determine the chance of survival; the residents along the coast may either rescue the survivors or fight for the floating goods first.

The rules of the sea ultimately have to withstand wet ropes, bad water and sudden turns of weather.
